title: Glossary of the terms this site uses
summary: The words this site uses for R.E.P.O. in plain language, each with a note on which part of the game it comes from so you can match it to what you see while playing.
body: We keep a small vocabulary. Where the game has its own word for something, this site uses that word rather than inventing a new one, so a name here matches a name you have already seen.
A run means one trip into a level and back out again, not a whole session. The game separates an ordinary level from a run level, which is why the word is used deliberately here.

The cart is the crew's hauling vehicle rather than a shopping trolley. It is an object with its own driving behaviour, which is why entries about the cart talk about speed and tilt rather than about wheels.

A monster state is what a monster is doing at that moment, not what kind of monster it is. Being stunned and despawning sit in the same list, which is why a stun is described here as a state rather than an interruption.
A trap valuable is a valuable that does something when it is disturbed. That is a different thing from a valuable that is simply worth money, which is why they are separate entries.
A module is one piece of a level, assembled by the generator rather than placed by hand, and the extraction point is the way out rather than a button you press.
Where we cannot match a word to one of the game's own, we say so instead of guessing. The technical reference shows how each term was checked for anyone who wants to see the working.

facts.claim: A run means one trip into a level and back out, not a whole session.
The cart is the crew's hauling vehicle rather than a shopping trolley.
A monster state is what a monster is doing, not what kind of monster it is.
A trap valuable is a valuable that does something when disturbed.
A module is one piece of a level assembled by the generator.
The extraction point is the way out rather than a button.
An upgrade here means an item rather than a number going up.
